title: Cargo-Lite 2.0 ships a shared build cache
summary: Rust build tool Cargo-Lite released version 2.0 with a shared, content-addressed build cache.
text: Cargo-Lite 2.0 was released on Tuesday. The headline feature is a shared build cache keyed by the content hash of each crate and its flags, so a team shares compiled artifacts across machines. One company reported that clean builds dropped from 41 minutes to 6. The old TOML configuration format still works in 2.x but is removed in 3.0; a migration command rewrites it. The cache can live on local disk or on any S3-compatible bucket.

title: Annual Rust survey: compile times still the top complaint
summary: For the fifth year, slow compile times lead the list of complaints in the annual Rust survey.
text: The annual Rust survey collected 9,800 responses. Compile times were named as the biggest pain point by 61 percent, ahead of async complexity (38 percent) and learning curve (31 percent). Respondents who use a shared build cache reported 40 percent lower dissatisfaction with build times. The survey authors note that the sample skews toward professional users.

title: Kubernetes 1.36 upgrade breaks pod networking on legacy CNI
summary: Clusters still on the legacy CNI plugin lose pod-to-pod networking after upgrading to 1.36.
text: Several operators reported that upgrading to Kubernetes 1.36 broke pod networking on clusters that still use the legacy CNI plugin. The 1.36 release notes list the plugin as removed, but the upgrade pre-flight check did not flag it. A workaround is to install a maintained CNI before the upgrade. The maintainers said a pre-flight warning will ship in 1.36.1.

title: Report: most Kubernetes workloads over-request CPU by 2x
summary: A study of 400 clusters finds requests far above actual usage.
text: A study of 400 production clusters found that the median workload requests 2.1 times the CPU it uses at the 95th percentile. The authors estimate 30 to 40 percent of node spend is idle headroom. Vertical autoscaling in recommendation mode reduced the gap to 1.3x in a pilot of 20 clusters without a single throttling incident.

title: Postmortem: payments database down 4 hours after one long transaction
summary: A single long-running transaction held a lock that cascaded into a full outage.
text: The postmortem describes a nightly report query that ran inside a transaction for 51 minutes, holding a lock on the payments table. Writers queued, connection pools filled, and the API returned errors for four hours. Fixes: statement timeouts of 30 seconds on application roles, the report moved to a read replica, and an alert on transactions older than five minutes.

title: SQLite 3.52 adds native vector search
summary: The new release ships a built-in vector index for embeddings.
text: SQLite 3.52 includes a vector index type that stores float32 embeddings and answers nearest-neighbor queries with cosine or L2 distance. The developers position it for applications with up to a few million vectors that already keep their data in SQLite. Benchmarks in the announcement show query times under 10 milliseconds for one million 768-dimensional vectors on a laptop.

title: Credential dump exposes 12 million passwords from Lumen breach
summary: Passwords from the Lumen fintech breach appeared on a public forum.
text: A file containing 12 million email and password pairs from the Lumen breach was posted on a public forum. Lumen says the passwords were hashed with bcrypt and that it has forced a reset for all accounts. Security researchers recommend users who reused the password elsewhere change it. The company has not said how the attackers got in.

title: CVE-2026-1234: OpenSSH agent forwarding RCE patched
summary: A remote code execution bug in the agent forwarding path is fixed in the latest release.
text: CVE-2026-1234 allows a malicious server to execute code on a client that connects with agent forwarding enabled. The fix is in the latest OpenSSH release; distributions have shipped backports. Until updated, users should disable agent forwarding. The bug was found by a security team during a routine audit and no exploitation in the wild has been reported.

title: Typosquatted PyPI package mimicked a popular HTTP library
summary: A malicious package with a one-letter name difference stole environment variables for three days.
text: A package whose name differed by one letter from a popular HTTP client library was downloaded about 4,000 times over three days before removal. On install it read environment variables and sent them to a remote server. PyPI has since added the name to its blocklist. The incident renews calls for lockfiles with hashes and for installing from a private mirror.

title: Small 3B model matches last year's frontier models on coding
summary: A compact open model reaches 2025 frontier scores on two coding benchmarks.
text: A 3-billion-parameter open-weights model scored within two points of last year's frontier models on two coding benchmarks. The authors attribute the result to training data curation rather than scale. Independent evaluators noted the benchmarks are public and may have leaked into training data, and are preparing a private test set.

title: Study: LLM judges prefer longer answers regardless of correctness
summary: An eval suite finds a systematic length bias in model-as-judge setups.
text: An open evaluation suite compared judge models against human labels on 2,000 answer pairs. Judges preferred the longer answer 68 percent of the time when the two answers were equally correct, and 41 percent of the time when the longer answer was wrong. Swapping the order of the pair changed the verdict in 12 percent of cases. The authors recommend explicit length instructions and order randomization.

title: Prompt caching cuts inference bills by 60 percent for retrieval-heavy workloads
summary: Teams that keep a stable prompt prefix report large savings.
text: A survey of twenty teams running retrieval-augmented applications found that moving static instructions and documents to the start of the prompt, and keeping that prefix byte-identical between calls, cut input token bills by 55 to 65 percent through provider-side prefix caching. The main failure mode was a timestamp or request id placed early in the prompt, which invalidated the cache on every call.

title: GPU shortage eases as two new fabs come online
summary: Fabs in Arizona and Dresden start volume production.
text: Two new fabs began volume production this month, one in Arizona and one in Dresden. Analysts expect lead times for data-center GPUs to fall from 36 weeks to about 20 by early next year. Spot prices for last-generation cards have already dropped 15 percent. Demand from AI training clusters remains the main driver.

title: Crewed lunar landing slips to 2029 after heat shield review
summary: A review of heat shield test data pushes the landing by a year.
text: The space agency announced that the crewed lunar landing is now planned for 2029. A review of heat shield data from the last uncrewed flight found uneven charring that engineers want to understand before flying people. The uncrewed test flight in 2027 is unaffected. Contractors said the delay adds about 400 million dollars to the program.

title: Battery recycling plant recovers 95 percent of lithium from EV packs
summary: A new facility reaches commercial scale with a hydrometallurgical process.
text: The plant processes 20,000 tonnes of spent electric-vehicle batteries a year and recovers 95 percent of the lithium, 98 percent of the nickel and cobalt, using a water-based process at low temperature. The operator says recovered materials cost 20 percent less than mined equivalents at current prices. Capacity is expected to double in 2028.

title: Cloud startup Nimbus lays off 30 percent after missing revenue targets
summary: The company cut 180 roles and narrowed its product line.
text: Nimbus, a cloud infrastructure startup, laid off 180 employees, about 30 percent of its staff, after missing its revenue target for the second quarter in a row. The company said it will focus on its managed database product and stop selling its edge network service. Customers of the edge service have six months to migrate.

title: Helm 4 released with OCI-only chart distribution
summary: The new major version drops classic chart repositories.
text: Helm 4 distributes charts only through OCI registries and removes support for the classic HTTP chart repository index. Values files gain an optional typed schema that the client validates before rendering. Charts built for Helm 3 install without changes, but repositories must be migrated to a registry.

title: Perovskite solar panels reach 30 percent efficiency in outdoor tests
summary: Tandem cells hold their output after a year outdoors.
text: Tandem perovskite-silicon panels reached 30.1 percent efficiency in a twelve-month outdoor test, retaining 97 percent of their initial output. Degradation under humidity, the technology's historical weakness, was reduced with a new encapsulation. Commercial production is planned for 2028 at a single factory.

title: Passkeys overtake SMS codes as second factor at major banks
summary: Six of the ten largest banks now default to passkeys.
text: Six of the ten largest banks in the survey now default new customers to passkeys rather than SMS one-time codes. Account takeover fraud at those banks fell 70 percent year over year. The remaining banks cited support costs for customers who lose devices as the reason for keeping SMS as the default.

title: Open eval suite: judge verdicts flip in 12 percent of swapped pairs
summary: Position bias measured directly by swapping answer order.
text: In the same evaluation suite that measured length bias, swapping the order of two candidate answers flipped the judge's verdict in 12 percent of pairs. The effect was larger for weaker judge models and nearly disappeared when the judge was asked to score each answer separately against a rubric before comparing.
